There are no network downloads at build time, no encoded commands, no exfiltration of local data, and no execution of untrusted fetched content. <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a single source entry pointing to a release tarball hosted on GitHub at the project's official repository. The URL is constructed using the package version and name, which is standard practice. During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, this source will be downloaded and extracted, but no build or prepare steps will be executed.

The top-level scope of the PKGBUILD contains no command substitutions or immediate execution of dangerous code. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so no dynamic version calculation occurs. The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, indicating the source integrity is intended to be verified, though even if it were set to 'SKIP', that would not make this stage unsafe.

No code in the global scope or in `pkgver()` performs network requests, file operations, or execution of external payloads. The potentially sensitive operations (like `sed`, `cmake`, etc.) are confined to the `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions, which are not executed under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. Therefore, sourcing the PKGBUILD and downloading the source is safe.
</details>
<evidence>

No malicious execution during source fetch and parse

The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build process for the `azahar` 3DS emulator, a fork of Citra. The build process uses standard CMake workflows, with dependencies resolved via system libraries where appropriate. This is a common workaround and not malicious.

No suspicious operations such as network access, data exfiltration, or execution of downloaded code are present. All modifications are confined to the build environment and intended installation paths. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices and poses no evidence of supply-chain compromise.
